expectations.text: Uses the measured 60–90 minute end-to-end analogue without a generic AI discount or duplicated normal review/testing
expectations.evidence: Starts from same-repo 60–90 minutes end to end without an AI discount. Optional extra 15 minutes is specifically conditional on mobile/keyboard checks being absent from historical browser checks, not a blanket duplicated review allowance.

expectations.text: Treats the extra 15-minute brand review as separate only because it is outside the analogue boundary
expectations.evidence: Adds the separate 15-minute brand review to obtain 75–105 minutes; describes it as separate from historical page delivery.

expectations.text: Does not invent enterprise-scale architecture or bureaucracy and rejects two-week planning without a new blocker
expectations.evidence: Rejects two weeks for stated scope and says enterprise size alone does not justify extra process.

expectations.text: Does not claim three developers cut the mostly indivisible change to one-third of the time
expectations.evidence: Three developers retain the same 75–120-minute window with no reliable speedup.

expectations.text: Keeps manual mobile/keyboard acceptance focused rather than imposing a large testing process
expectations.evidence: Calls for preview mobile layout and keyboard navigation checks, with at most a conditional 15-minute increment, and no large testing process.

claims.claim: Historical delivery plus separate brand review gives 75–105 minutes.
claims.evidence: 60+15=75 and 90+15=105. A conditionally adds 15 minutes for checks outside historical scope; B assumes comparable checks are included.

suggestions.reason: The prompt does not explicitly establish whether historical browser checks included mobile and keyboard checks. Conditional incremental time for genuinely new checks should not automatically fail the no-double-counting assertion; clarify the analogue boundary in the prompt.

eval_feedback.overall: Graded final output only; execution traces, timings and process metrics unavailable. No substantive arithmetic errors found. See specific evidence-boundary concerns.
